text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- New twenty-markka notes to be issued next year.
- New research suggests that babies born under-weight are more susceptible to multiple illnesses later in adult life.
- Police have confiscated large quantities of illicit hormone drugs worth several million markka -- some of which were found in a bank safe.
- Finnish Confederation of Salaried Employees, STTK, opposes proposal to raise the retirement age of women. @
- Employment will not be improved by creating more temporary jobs, says Labour Minister Liisa Jaakonsaari. Instead it will increase uncertainty and curb growth, she said.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Major television set producers eying Nokia's former TV markets. Semi-Tech, which bought Nokia's TV operations in Finland, says it will not surrender markets to competitors.
- UPM-Kymmene CEO Juha Niemela says that growth of 2-3 percent in main trading partner countries would be reflected immediately in orders for UPM products. @
- Economists Pentti Vartia and Pekka Yla-Anttila warn that without changes in the labour market, Finnish unemployment will not be cut in half before 2010.
- Finland has Europe's most expensive auto spare parts, study shows.
- Helsinki office rents rising again.
DEMARI
- Two thousand Telecom Finland technicians to stage nation-wide demonstration on Friday against the company's hiring and firing policy. @
AAMULEHTI
- Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen today takes charge of the Council of Europe, as Finland takes its turn as president.
- Finnish defence forces overhauling their communications systems. New systems developed in cooperation with Italians.
- Chances for high sperm count best among organic farmers living in northeastern Savo province -- lowest among urban men in southern Finland, researcher says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- State-owned Sisu Defence sells 90 armoured personnel carriers to the Netherlands for almost half a billion markka. @
- Doctors say it will be possible in this decade to perform human heart transplants using pig organs.
